comments.body:
## Filtered remediation register

The survey covered 3,222 tracked files at repository commit `8fa8f36b6482b2371128607a63c5483a9783e887`. The register below incorporates the external documentation survey, the comment and embedded prose survey, implementation checks, historical record checks, and three challenge filters. Project files remain unchanged.

The external and comment shards returned reports. The dedicated internal-records agent did not deliver a final response during adjudication. Root verification and recorded internal checkpoints supplied the cited internal evidence. The completed cross-shard filters also reviewed that evidence.

P0 identifies false guidance, missing user discovery, or missing policy controls that can cause incorrect operation. P1 identifies audience, completeness, maintainability, or current-state defects. P2 identifies bounded cleanup or research that must precede a prescriptive change.

## Foundation and enforcement

- F01 P0 Documentation ownership policy. Add `docs/documentation-policy.md` with the audience matrix, lifecycle, canonical source rules, citation rules, generated artifact rules, historical correction procedures, exclusions, and examples. Keep ticket events append-only and preserve ADR decision substance through annotations or errata. Link to it from `docs/README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `AGENTS.md`.
- F02 P0 Maintained prose remediation. Review maintained authored prose through its canonical source and apply the punctuation, diction, formal voice, and paragraph rules. Protect code syntax, technical identifiers, tables, licenses, quotations, captures, frozen model output, serialized fixtures, and wording under test.
- F03 P0 Prose validation. Add a source-aware checker for maintained Markdown, help, narration, package and server metadata, YAML, TOML, HCL, shell text, workflow annotations, and schema descriptions. Fail on deterministic prohibited forms and report meaning-sensitive candidates for manual review. Manual review covers structural colons, adjective necessity, formal voice, and paragraph classification. Integrate the checker with the Makefile and a portable CI path. Add authoring-time validation or lint guidance for new ticket prose, ADR prose, session logs, and commit messages. Preserve structural commit trailers and do not rewrite historical ticket events or commits.
- F04 P0 Comment policy and validation. Expand `scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` beyond selected Python trees. A ticket or ADR citation may support rationale but must not exempt historical narration. Add format-aware exclusions and retain manual judgment for comment necessity.
- F05 P1 Generated source ownership. Record the canonical source, generator, derived outputs, and drift check for configuration reference, ADR index, CLI reference, MCP reference, synchronized templates, schemas, and demonstration assets. Establish ownership before changing an artifact that has no identified source.
- F06 P1 Documentation navigation. Rewrite `docs/README.md` as one landing page with labeled client, contributor, architecture, ADR, operations, research, and evidence routes. Correct the relation count and classify historical artifacts before relocation.
- F07 P1 Documentation index validation. Expand `scripts/check_docs_index.py` beyond top-level page membership and links under `docs`. Cover maintained documentation and runbook roots, document the checker boundary, and detect broken internal links outside `docs`.

## External documentation and shipped help

- F08 P0 Client README. Preserve the tested quickstart, merge the duplicate installation sections, and retain installation, first use, core concepts, supported interfaces, and client navigation. Correct the seven relations, `caused_by`, the optional `unlink` relation, and completion checks for ordinary task and bug closes. Move contributor process, implementation design, gate internals, source paths, and test tiers to internal documentation.
- F09 P0 Operation certificate guidance. Correct `README.md`, `docs/manifest-signing.md`, `docs/event-schema.md`, `docs/reuse-surface.md`, `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md`, `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `docs/sample-ticket-log.jsonl`, `src/rebar/_cli/help/sign.txt`, and derived CLI text. Describe DSSE envelopes signed through SSHSIG for plan review and completion verification. Classify every HMAC reference and preserve HMAC only for compatibility, cookie, webhook, or other implemented consumers. Do not include `docs/llm-framework.md` in this defect set.
- F10 P0 Import guidance. Rewrite `src/rebar/_cli/help/import.txt` and `docs/import-export.md`, then regenerate derived help. Document idempotency keyed by `source_id`, chunk commits, deferred push, partial results, reruns, crash recovery, and the conditions that can create duplicates.
- F11 P0 CLI option coverage. Add `--detected-by` to create help. Add `--caused-by` and `--ref` to transition usage and option guidance. Verify relation attribution, close verification, structured output, errors, and regenerated reference text against parser and command tests.
- F12 P1 CLI command discovery. Coordinate top-level discovery and generated reference wording with `grapy-cynical-copepod`, `premium-drizzly-weaverbird`, `loony-fabric-bunny`, and `pettish-snippy-rasbora`. Verify the routed explain, review, verification, scan, and workflow families after their registry work lands. Do not introduce another parser or generator path.
- F13 P1 MCP summaries. Preserve complete concise registrar descriptions in `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py`, correct transition close semantics at the registrar source, and regenerate `docs/mcp-reference.md`. Keep input schemas, output schemas, errors, and stable tool names aligned with registration tests.
- F14 P1 Server manifest descriptions. Extend `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` to validate environment descriptions and other maintained client text, not only environment names. Correct the canonical manifest text before regenerating or publishing derived metadata.
- F15 P0 Adoption templates. Correct `templates/AGENTS.md`, `templates/rebar-usage.md`, and synchronized regions. Teach atomic claim, configured default assignment, Jira-resolvable overrides, dependency-order review, seven relations, supported identifiers, and correct close classification.
- F16 P0 Demonstration assets. Establish the source and regeneration contract for `docs/assets/rebar-demo.svg` and related narration. Correct bare assignees, deprecated identifiers, relation coverage, review outcomes, and close behavior in the maintained source.
- F17 P0 Example agent workflows. Correct `examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md` and `examples/agent-skills/rebar-brainstorm/SKILL.md` where they teach non-atomic claims, transient bare identities, incomplete relation sets, deprecated references, or unsigned fast failures as success. Mark repository-specific workflows when portability does not apply.
- F18 P1 User guide. Organize `docs/user-guide.md` by client goals. Cover supported ticket, session log, metrics, import, export, bridge, and recovery workflows. Add `caused_by` and remove router mechanics, blame selection, credential incident history, and other implementation narration.
- F19 P0 Configuration guidance. Make generated `docs/config-reference.md` the external settings contract. Keep extension and ownership invariants in internal configuration documentation. Remove future plans, reconcile examples, and correct the cross-ticket overlap link to ADR 0086 and the transport retry link to ADR 0087.
- F20 P0 Identity setup. Correct the `GITHUB_ENV` claim in `docs/identity-setup.md`. Name `verify-identity` as canonical and `verify-authorship` as a compatibility alias. State that `session_log`, `code_review`, and `identity` are the exact exempt types. Document secure propagation, verification, rotation, failure handling, and project-neutral examples.
- F21 P0 Jira operator setup. Rewrite `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` as an operator checklist. Require project selection through `rebar bridge projects set`, validate `JIRA_PROJECT` before synchronization, remove the unsupported `DIG` fallback, and cover prerequisites, first synchronization, observation, recovery, rollback, and limitations. Remove project-specific bot identities from copied workflows.
- F22 P1 Jira development tools. Repair or retire `scripts/jira-onboarding-reference` and `scripts/jira-pressure-test` material. Replace deleted command paths, remove implemented work from future plans, and keep developer harness instructions separate from client setup.
- F23 P1 Plan-writing guide. Keep `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` focused on description structure, acceptance criteria, dependency order, review, remediation, status checks, and claim. Keep reviewer design and criterion routing in `docs/plan-review-gate.md` and `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`.
- F24 P1 Connector-limited workflow. Rewrite `docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md` as one environment detection, fallback payload, sanctioned import, validation, recovery, and escalation sequence. Resolve the conflicting `fsck` and `validate` guidance.
- F25 P1 Exit-code reference. Keep `docs/exit-codes.md` limited to current exit meanings, retry guidance, stable output effects, and recovery. Move gate chronology to tickets or ADRs.
- F26 P1 Release communication. Keep `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/release-notes.md` focused on user-visible behavior, compatibility, migrations, and upgrade effects. Move execution chronology and implementation measurements to tickets.
- F27 P1 Public library documentation. Add client-facing function docstrings for `unlink`, `tag`, `untag`, `archive`, and `compact` in `src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py`. Document parameters, return values, mutation effects, repository selection, relation behavior, and errors from wrappers and tests. Align `docs/reuse-surface.md`.
- F28 P1 Support, security, conduct, and reporting. Align `SUPPORT.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `GOVERNANCE.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, issue forms, contact links, and `infra/runbooks/github-mirror-lock.md`. Preserve the Nava PBC backstop, clarify the shared address and unnamed escalation owner, provide private security reporting, and retain GitHub Issues and Actions when client support and the Verified gate depend on them.
- F29 P1 Contributor workflow. Make `CONTRIBUTING.md` canonical. Reduce `AGENTS.md`, `docs/your-first-change.md`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, and other entry points to audience-specific constraints and pointers. Correct hook setup, Gerrit landing, pull request expectations, flake handling, and Makefile help. Replace duplicated ticket relation counts with a pointer to the canonical ticket model.

## Internal current-state documentation and durable records

- F30 P1 Architecture. Rewrite `docs/architecture.md` from implemented subsystem boundaries, dependency direction, data ownership, public seams, and extension points. Label ADR 0098 and ADR 0100 by implementation state and remove module-split chronology from current architecture.
- F31 P1 Event contract. Rewrite `docs/event-schema.md` from the schema registry and event models. Include current ticket types, event kinds, certificate envelopes, compatibility reads, and extension rules. Move retired writer history to tickets.
- F32 P1 Concurrency and synchronization. Rewrite `docs/concurrency.md` from current Python writers, optimistic concurrency, parent-first cascades, shared writes, recovery, and tracker maintenance. Remove deleted shell writer references and retain safety constraints.
- F33 P1 Migration registry. Keep `docs/migrations.md` focused on the idempotent ensure registry, supported migration state, ordering, recovery, and extension rules. Move rollout chronology and completed proof to tickets.
- F34 P0 ADR lifecycle. Define the minimum metadata needed for status, date, decision relationships, implementation state, and applicability. Include owner and ticket references where the policy requires them. Correct the ADR 0042, ADR 0047, ADR 0090, and ADR 0091 relationship defects through annotations or errata that preserve decision substance and prior status history. Extend `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` and make `scripts/gen_adr_index.py` emit normalized metadata with conforming prose and paragraph shape.
- F35 P1 Completed plans and evidence. Classify every item under `docs/archive`, `docs/design`, `docs/research`, `docs/experiments`, migration records, validation records, and named remediation plans. Preserve unique chronology on tickets, preserve frozen evidence with provenance, retain maintained procedures, and promote governing batch-runner invariants to ADR 0003 or a new ADR after implementation confirmation.
- F36 P1 Runbook boundaries. Review each infrastructure runbook separately. Keep prerequisites, commands, validation, observation, rollback, recovery, and safety constraints. Move decision rationale to ADRs and completed handoffs, incidents, cutover proof, and measurements to tickets.
- F37 P0 Jira backend narration. Correct comments and internal prose that name only `jira` or describe Jira Data Center, ACLI, ADF, or shared sanitization as future work. Document the `jira` and `jira-datacenter` registrations, shared contracts, backend differences, and extension boundaries.
- F38 P0 Maintenance policy accuracy. Correct `docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md` so the 800 line module limit is absolute and sourced from `.github/module-size-limit.txt`. Remove dated tool availability and baseline narration from the maintained procedure.

## Comments, executable prose, and presentation text

- F39 P1 Contextual comment remediation. Build an exact file and symbol inventory before editing production, script, test, workflow, Terraform, Dockerfile, Makefile, configuration, and shell comments. Keep current invariants, ownership, ordering, safety, failure semantics, concurrency, compatibility, unusual fixtures, and regression rationale. Move chronology to tickets or ADRs. Remove restatements and ornamental dividers only after contextual review.
- F40 P1 Prompts, evaluations, and schemas. Treat reviewer prompts, routing data, and evaluation specifications as internal executable prose. Treat client-visible schema descriptions as external contracts. Rewrite canonical sources while preserving identifiers, scoring meaning, schemas, fixtures, and oracles. Replace the stale fixed claim of 41 prompts with a derived inventory.
- F41 P1 Diagnostics and presentation text. Rewrite confirmed exception messages, logs, command output, Makefile help, workflow annotations, audit display text, shell help, and spoken narration. When text reports a failure, state the cause and next action. Preserve error codes, field names, structured markers, compatibility tokens, and wording fixtures.
- F42 P2 Research and experiment records. Inventory every procedure and corpus before classification. Keep purpose, inputs, outputs, safety, environment, and reproduction in maintained procedures. Put outcomes and follow-up on tickets, cite decisive evidence from ADRs, and add provenance, digest, tool version, and applicability metadata to frozen artifacts without rewriting them.

## Operator documentation and provenance

- F43 P0 MCP authentication operations. Correct `src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py`, `docs/mcp-auth.md`, `infra/terraform/modules/sso-gate/README.md`, and the maintained authentication runbook. Document the five supported verifier strategies, prerequisites, secrets, deployment, validation, observation, rollback, recovery, and the correct runbook path.
- F44 P1 S3 operations. Review `docs/s3-backend.md` and related operational prose for audience, setup, validation, observation, recovery, rollback, and conformance. Do not assert an S3 accuracy defect unless implementation evidence establishes one.
- F45 P0 Gerrit operations. Correct `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md`, `infra/runbooks/two-vote-gate-rollback.md`, Gerrit configuration guidance, and related workflows. State the effective Verified requirement, current paths, prerequisites, validation, rollback, and recovery. Move rollout and incident history to tickets.
- F46 P1 Package license inclusion. Include `docs/licenses/adjective-adjective-animal-LICENSE.txt` in the distribution path used by `pyproject.toml`. Decide the required `NOTICE` treatment after confirming the distribution contents and license obligations.
- F47 P2 Legacy wordlist provenance. Research the source and license of the packaged legacy ticket wordlist before adding provenance metadata or prescribing redistribution terms.
- F48 P2 Jira Data Center fixture provenance. Research the upstream revision and license for `tests/external/live_jira_dc/Dockerfile` before adding a pin, attribution, or license statement.
- F49 P1 Package and example metadata. Review package descriptions, classifiers, project URLs, server metadata, and example indexes for client usefulness and maintained destinations. Add the required `name` field to `examples/agent-skills/rebar-brainstorm/SKILL.md` and validate all example skill metadata and paths.

## Adjudication and implementation boundaries

No confirmed correction was rejected. C14 merged into the Jira operator setup work. C29 and C30 merged into contextual comment remediation. C32 merged into comment policy and contextual review. C33 split into MCP authentication, S3, and Gerrit work. C34 split into package license inclusion, legacy wordlist research, Jira Data Center fixture research, and example metadata. Other draft items were retained or revised for evidence accuracy, audience, canonical-source ownership, or scope.

Use `educatory-astrakhan-wallaroo` and `decorative-childly-auk` for signing history, `cold-stall-chalk` for import history, `selenium-pugnacious-arcticduck` for comment hygiene, `vein-acid-navy` for Jira onboarding, `sullen-famished-incatern` for plan review retry guidance, and `peak-fir-hilt`, `knotty-hat-chase`, and `unfed-posse-urn` for batch-runner history. Preserve the quickstart and generated-reference work from `tsunamic-wax-hog`. Reference these records from current documentation only when their history explains a maintained invariant.

Historical ticket events and commit messages remain unchanged. Ticket corrections use append-only comments or linked notices. Licenses, quotations, captures, frozen output, serialized fixtures, technical syntax, and wording fixtures remain protected. Generated outputs change through canonical sources. Decomposition must group overlapping file changes by canonical source and order derived output after source changes. P0 accuracy and ownership work precedes structural cleanup. Provenance research precedes license or attribution prescriptions. Implementation remains pending operator approval.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The project needs a repository-wide audit of documentation and source comments against the operator standards recorded below. Future developers and agents need an evidence-based remediation proposal before any project file changes are authorized.

## Audit standards

The standards baseline is the operator instruction dated 2026-08-20, preserved in this ticket through the following requirements.

- Prose must not use an em dash, en dash, spaced hyphen, semicolon, or a colon that connects or introduces a clause within a sentence.
- A colon may introduce a list of items or act as a structural label. Spoken narration must contain no colon.
- Hyphens are limited to compound words, technical names, identifiers, Markdown list bullets, table separators, horizontal rules, code operators, or SQL operators. A plain hyphen must not replace a dash.
- Every Markdown paragraph remains one logical line. Line breaks remain only where Markdown structure requires them.
- Writing uses a formal voice with precise verbs, complete sentences, no contractions, no colloquialisms, and no casual connectors.
- Filler or authenticity padding must be deleted. The prohibited filler list contains `real`, `actual`, `genuine`, `live` when used as a value adjective, `simply`, `just`, `quietly`, `seamlessly`, `robust`, `powerful`, `leverage`, `truly`, `in real time`, `concretely`, and `today` when used for emphasis rather than as a date.
- Authenticity padding phrases such as `not a placeholder`, `live for this run`, `the thing that matters`, or `this is not a mock` must not appear. Writing describes the mechanism or source instead of claiming authenticity.
- A noun remains unmodified unless an adjective selects one option from several.
- Tickets preserve the history of work for future developers or agents.
- ADRs preserve key decisions that introduce architectural invariants needing more visibility than tickets. Future developers or agents are their primary audience.
- Internal project documentation explains the current development processes, architecture, or codebase. It references tickets or ADRs when historical context is necessary instead of repeating material that has no future use.
- External documentation teaches clients who do not develop rebar or understand its internals. It uses concise language focused on using rebar.
- Shipped help follows the external documentation model. It supports discovery and directs users to relevant information shipped with rebar.
- Comments provide developer context required to understand code. Comments are not conversations, historical records, or restatements of the code. References to tickets or ADRs are encouraged when they supply necessary context.

## Approach

Build a complete textual-surface inventory from `rg --files`, file-type grouping, Python tokenization, and targeted searches. Apply the shard precedence rules below so each surface has one exploration owner. Compare factual claims with code, configuration, generated help sources, tests, ADRs, and relevant ticket history. Each agent returns a structured report to the root agent. The root agent alone appends report summaries to the session log. The separation between exploration and adversarial validation follows the sequence in `docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md`. The content-specific shard map below is defined for this audit because that runbook uses code-health perspectives rather than documentation surfaces. Separate exploration owners reduce omissions within large surface families. The later challenge pass evaluates the complete set, which exposes cross-shard duplication, misplacement, unsupported claims, and coverage gaps.

## Exploration shard map

- **Shard A. Durable records plus internal documentation.** This shard owns ADRs, architecture documents, development process documents, contributor governance documents, research records, experiments, archives, design notes, infrastructure runbooks, test READMEs, and relevant ticket history. It owns each standalone document not assigned to shard B.
- **Shard B. External documentation plus shipped help.** This shard owns the root client overview, support or security guidance, user guides, command references, configuration references, integration setup, examples, templates, packaged guides, files under `src/rebar/_cli/help/`, client-facing CLI strings, client-facing MCP descriptions, and package documentation metadata.
- **Shard C. Developer comments plus embedded prose.** This shard owns comments or docstrings in source, scripts, tests, experiment code, workflows, configuration, and infrastructure. It also owns reviewer prompts, schema descriptions, error text, or other embedded prose not assigned to shard B.
- **Precedence rule.** A client-facing string belongs to shard B. A comment or docstring belongs to shard C. A standalone document belongs to shard A unless shard B names its audience as clients. The root coverage table records the owner of every surface group, so mixed files do not create overlapping review responsibility.

## Filtering pass

After consolidation, three agents receive the complete draft list. One challenges evidence plus factual accuracy. One challenges taxonomy, placement, completeness, plus duplication. One challenges punctuation, diction, paragraph shape, audience fit, plus concision. The root adjudicates each item as retained, revised, merged, or rejected.

## Scope

- Root contributor and client documents, package metadata, repository policies, templates, and workflow text.
- Internal documents under `docs/`, including ADRs and indexes.
- External documents, packaged guides, command help, MCP descriptions, examples, and other shipped user guidance.
- Developer comments and docstrings in maintained source, scripts, tests, and configuration files.
- Relevant ticket history needed to distinguish historical records from current-state documentation.
- Generated corpora, dependency content, caches, build output, wordlists, binary assets, and archived machine output receive inventory entries plus provenance checks rather than line-level prose review.
- Read-only repository inspection. No project file edits, gates, commits, or pushes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The inventory names every maintained surface in scope plus every explicit exclusion. Verification uses a session log coverage table.
- [ ] Every proposal cites a repository path, symbol, command output, ADR, or ticket as evidence. Verification uses the proposal evidence field.
- [ ] Every proposal names one target documentation type plus its audience. Verification uses the proposal classification fields.
- [ ] Every proposal states one remediation action plus one destination. Verification uses the proposal action fields.
- [ ] Every factual correction identifies the implementation, configuration, test, or effective help source used to establish expected behavior. Verification uses the proposal citations.
- [ ] Exploration agents inspect the three shard definitions. Verification uses one session log report for each shard.
- [ ] Filtering agents challenge every consolidated proposal for evidence quality, factual accuracy, completeness, placement, duplication, plus prose conformance. Verification assigns every draft item a retained, revised, merged, or rejected status.
- [ ] The final proposal text conforms to the audit standards in this ticket. Verification applies the pattern set `\x{2014}|\x{2013}|\x20\x2d\x20|\x3b|\x3a` plus manual diction review to the draft text before storage.
- [ ] No project file changes exist at handoff. Verification uses final worktree status plus diff checks.
- [ ] The filtered proposal appears in a ticket comment. Verification uses `rebar show minimum-rainy-fawn`.
- [ ] The filtered proposal appears in the operator response. Verification uses the completed response.
